transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I'm an EMT, and my supervisor required me to get a psychiatric evaluation after pulling me off field duty. On calls, I feel like I'm moving wrong and doing the wrong things, like my actions don't match what's happening around me, and my crew says I'm acting really off.
When this happens, do you still know that the feeling is coming from your own mind, or do you actually believe something outside you is controlling your actions or that people are trying to harm you?

I don't feel like an outside force is physically controlling me, but when I freeze, it's like my body is on a different channel and I just can't snap out of it. However, I do believe people are targeting me, because I'm convinced dispatch and hospital staff are slipping coded messages into the radio and charts to track my mistakes and get me fired.

Before these beliefs and freezing episodes started, did you have any recent head injury, seizure, serious illness, or start/stop any drugs, alcohol, or medications? If so, what happened and when did it begin?

No, I don't have any history of head injuries, seizures, or serious illnesses, and I was physically uninjured in that big car accident. I also haven't changed any medications or started using any drugs or alcohol.
How long have the coded-message beliefs and the freezing episodes been going on, and did they start suddenly or build up over time?

The freezing and acting off started gradually after a bad multi-car pileup I responded to on I-95 about ten months ago, slowly building up over the past year. The feeling about the coded messages is much more recent, though, and has only been happening for the last couple of months.
Since that pileup, have you had unwanted memories, nightmares, or flashbacks of it, and do you avoid reminders of the crash? Also, do you feel constantly on edge or easily startled since then?
No, I haven't really had any nightmares or flashbacks about the crash, and I don't find myself trying to avoid reminders of it. I also don't feel constantly on edge or easily startled since then.

For the belief that dispatch and hospital staff are sending you coded messages, has that belief been present almost every day for more than 3 months, or did it come on suddenly and stay under 3 months so far?
No, it hasn't been going on for more than three months. That belief about the coded messages is pretty recent and has only been happening for the last couple of months.

Besides the coded-message belief, have you had any other psychotic symptoms—like hearing voices, seeing things others don’t, or feeling your thoughts are being interfered with—and did all of these symptoms start within the same recent 2-month period?

No, I haven't heard any voices, seen things, or felt like my thoughts are being interfered with. It's really just been the belief about the coded messages in the radio and chart notes. That specific feeling is the only one I've had, and it started about two months ago.

When you notice the coded messages or the feeling that your body is on a different channel, are there times you can step back and think, "this might just be my mind reacting," or are you completely certain it is really happening? Which of those feels more true most of the time?

I am completely certain the coded messages are real and directed at me, even though my supervisor swears it's just routine paperwork. When my body is on a different channel, I know in the moment that I'm acting off, but I physically can't snap out of it or change what I'm doing, so it feels completely out of my control.

opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a recent-onset fixed persecutory delusion lasting less than 3 months, with abrupt psychotic symptoms emerging within the last 2 months and no evidence of substance use, medical/neurologic cause, or chronic psychotic syndrome. PTSD is not supported because trauma-related re-experiencing, avoidance, and hyperarousal were denied. Delusional disorder is less likely because the delusion duration is under 3 months.
